forks.decision: One evolutionary loop mutates code and text; a candidate is a commit
The loop engine is GEPA optimize_anything with repeat runs on frontier candidates
The loop may mutate only src and prompts; winners land as human-reviewed draft PRs
The judge labels per-task applicability and critiques each rollout for reflection only; grader correctness is the only objective
The Phase 4 power gate is retired; every paid run requires an explicit spend ceiling

contradictions: Interface sketches (spec line 100) + Contract Engine (line 44) + AC-12 pass `evolve.evaluate(candidate, task)` directly as the optimize_anything evaluator, but gepa 0.1.4 forwards the dataset item only as the keyword `example` and filters kwargs by the evaluator's parameter names (gepa/optimize_anything.py:1002-1044 EvaluatorWrapper: all_kwargs={"example": ...}, _filter_kwargs drops it, then evaluator_fn(eval_candidate, **filtered)); with a parameter named `task` the call becomes evaluate(candidate) and raises TypeError on the first evaluation (raise_on_exception defaults True, optimize_anything.py:468). The AC-12 test stubs optimize_anything, so it cannot catch this.

Contract Candidate (line 43), Proposer isolation (line 49) and Applier (lines 50-56): `src_patch` is the export's diff against the parent commit and materialize applies it in a worktree at the parent commit, but GEPA builds every child as parent_candidate.copy() updated only with the proposed components (gepa/proposer/reflective_mutation/reflective_mutation.py:517-518) and the spec keeps module_selector round_robin; so a text-only child of a parent with a non-empty src_patch inherits the parent's incremental patch and materialize re-applies it onto a commit that already contains it, failing the apply stage. The spec never says the dispatcher resets src_patch in text rounds or that src_patch is cumulative from the seed; AC-6's test_materialize_commits_text_and_patch only covers a fresh patch on its parent.

Contract Candidate (line 43) / Applier step 6 (line 56) vs Stop and finish (line 67): GEPA candidates form a tree (several children per parent), yet each candidate is 'one commit on the scratch branch evolve/<run-id>' whose parent is its GEPA parent's commit; one branch tip cannot hold a tree, and finish 'pushes evolve/<run-id>' and opens a PR 'whose head is the winner commit' although a `gh pr create --draft` head is a branch whose tip is whatever was committed last, not necessarily the winner. Nothing says the branch is reset to the winner before push or what the PR base is (the seed-to-winner diff needs a base at --seed-sha); the AC-10 tests use a stubbed PR client that accepts a sha as head.

Contract Cascade (line 58) records 'the tail of that stage's output' in side info on a failing stage, but Reflective record (line 45) says GEPA side info is built only from allowlisted records; a failing cheap-tier stage runs cells through run.py, whose cell loop prints correctness_reason to stdout (benchmark/run.py:1252 `print(f"  → {result['correctness_reason']}")`), which names missing required strings (benchmark/tasks/base.py:180) — so the stage-output tail leaks grader text into side info and the reflection/proposer prompts. No test exercises the cheap-tier failure side info for SECRET_GT.

Contract Reflective record (line 45) and AC-1 (line 113) make c5's allowlisted record the `judge.critique(row, trajectory)` input, but c4 builds its own stripped record from a raw row with a different allowlist (bench-model-judge.md:54 adds result_text, num_tool_calls, f2p_/p2p_ keys; c5 adds prompt) and withholds the critique unless the row carries `contaminated` exactly false and a `trajectory_path` (bench-model-judge.md:59) and keys its cache by `run_key`; c5's record excludes all three fields ('fields outside the allowlist never enter it'), so passing it makes every calibrated critique raise CritiqueWithheld('contaminated'), while passing the raw row contradicts AC-1. The AC-4 tests use a stub judge, so the seam break passes.

Contract Spend and auth (line 68) defines a judge call's estimate as 'the mean cost of earlier calls of the same kind in this run, else --cell-estimate-usd', but c4 makes its rule canonical and forbids callers from redefining it: 'mean recorded cost of cached calls of the same kind ..., else the largest judge call cost this run, else --cell-estimate-usd ... callers, c5 included, ... never re-define the judge-call estimate' (bench-model-judge.md:73).
acceptance_gaps: Contract Engine (line 44): the text-component reflection is a `claude -p` call with no stated cwd, tool restriction, MCP or settings isolation (unlike the proposer at line 49 or c4's judge argv `--tools "" --strict-mcp-config --setting-sources ""` in an empty temp dir), and no AC or test constrains it; a default `claude -p` started from the tilth checkout can Read/Grep benchmark/tasks/*.py ground truth and the Gin held-out tests, breaking the parent invariant that no optimizer-side model reads grader inputs (benchmark-gepa-overhaul.md:96), and AC-12's test_dispatcher_routes_components_without_litellm checks only routing.

Contract Proposer isolation (line 49) requires no MCP server, no settings sources, and a per-call Claude config dir that copies auth only, but AC-5's test_proposer_command_disables_tools only checks --tools, the Bash/WebFetch/WebSearch disallow list, and the absence of an MCP config flag; an implementation that omits --strict-mcp-config and --setting-sources "" and uses the host CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (loading user MCP servers, hooks and settings) passes every listed test.

Contract Stop and finish (line 67) picks finalists as the two best non-seed frontier candidates by dev mean and the winner by highest test-split mean (contaminated counted incorrect, ties by dev mean then earlier commit), but AC-10 never states the winner rule and no test checks finalist selection or that the non-seed finalist with the higher test mean wins; test_finish_no_pr_when_seed_wins and test_finish_opens_one_draft_for_nonseed_winner both pass for an implementation that PRs the best-dev candidate whenever it beats the seed on test.
